title: 32 rejects the LRM's own Example 7: an attribute after a function name is LEGAL
detail: VERIFIED. annex-a-syntax.html A.8.2: `analog_function_call ::= analog_function_identifier { attribute_instance } ( analog_expression {, analog_expression} )`. ch2-lexical.html 2.9: an attribute_instance 'can appear as a suffix to an operator or a Verilog-AMS function name in an expression', and Example 7 is `a = add (* mode="cla" *) (b, c);` verbatim. The fixture writes `twice (* mode="fast" *) (V(p))` and pins `//! reject DiagnosticsReported` with NO debt banner and the boilerplate comment 'normative syntax/restriction snapshot'. A CONFORMING compiler compiles this and FAILS the fixture. Its sibling 21 was already flipped the other way, so the chapter contradicts itself. This must become a must-run fixture; it will then FAIL until VerA parses the form, which is why ch02-04 is a prerequisite (verifyRuns has no xfail escape).
expected: Must-run fixture with ports and a value claim: analog function `twice(x)=2.0*x`, `//! bias V(p)=0.7`, `CHECKX("attribute after a function name is a suffix, not a call", twice (* mode="fast" *) (V(p)), 1.4)`. Cites `//! lrm 2.9` and `//! lrm A.8.2`. Delete 32_function_call_attribute.expected-error.txt.

title: 36 rejects the whitespace position 2.6.1 explicitly permits, and that the LRM spells in three of its own examples
detail: VERIFIED. 2.6.1: 'The unsigned number token shall immediately follow the base format, optionally preceded by white space.' The LRM writes it itself in Example 1 (`'h 837FF`), Example 2 (`5 'D 3`), Example 3 (`4 'shf`, `-8 'd 6`) and Example 5 (`32 'h 12ab_f001`). The fixture's own DEBT banner quotes rule VAMS-2.6.1-09 and admits the rejection is not conformance. A conforming compiler FAILS it. Probed: `8'h Af` and friends are what VerA refuses. Blocked on ch02-04 like ch02-01.
expected: Must-run: `x = 8'h Af + 8'b 1010 + 8'o 17 + 8'd 12;` with `CHECKI("8'h Af", 8'h Af, 175)`, `CHECKI("8'b 1010", 8'b 1010, 10)`, `CHECKI("8'o 17", 8'o 17, 15)`, `CHECKI("8'd 12", 8'd 12, 12)`, `CHECKI("sum", x, 212)` — identical wants to 35_uppercase_bases_hex.va, which passes today with the space removed, so the diff isolates exactly the whitespace rule. `//! lrm 2.6.1`. Delete the sidecar.

title: 37 rejects macro substitution that 2.6.1 declares legal in so many words
detail: VERIFIED. 2.6.1 first paragraph: a based constant 'shall be composed of up to three tokens — an optional size constant, an apostrophe character followed by a base format character, and the digits representing the value of the number. It shall be legal to macro substitute these three tokens.' The fixture defines `BASE 'h` and `DIGITS A5`, writes `8 `BASE `DIGITS`, and pins a rejection. Its own DEBT banner quotes VAMS-2.6.1-03. A conforming compiler FAILS it. Blocked on ch02-04.
expected: Must-run: `CHECKI("macro-substituted base and digit tokens", x, 165)` where `x = 8 `BASE `DIGITS` and 0xA5 = 165. `//! lrm 2.6.1`, `//! lrm 10.3`. Delete the sidecar.

title: verifyRuns ignores //! xfail, so no must-run fixture can be red-but-known — the three items above have no landing place
detail: VERIFIED by reading the source. verifyRejected (torture.zig:502-559) consults `d.xfail` in three places (:520 compiled-cleanly, :532 substring-missing, :550 XPASS-is-a-FAIL). verifyRuns (:697-836) never mentions `d.xfail`: a must-run fixture that VerA cannot compile returns `.fail` at the `did not compile` arm (:759). So `//! xfail` is reject-only, exactly as README documents ('`//! xfail` only makes sense next to `//! reject`'). Every one of ch02-01/02/03/05 states a rule the LRM makes LEGAL and VerA refuses — the reject direction is unavailable to them by construction. Without this change the only two dispositions are 'keep the anti-conformant reject' or 'take four hard FAILs'.
expected: Honour `//! xfail` in verifyRuns on the compile/codegen/testbench-build arms: print `XFAIL <path>: <reason>` and return `.xfail` instead of `.fail`, and keep the XPASS rule symmetric — if an xfail-marked must-run fixture compiles AND every assertion prints ok=1, that is a hard FAIL telling the author to delete the line. Update README's 'only makes sense next to //! reject' sentence.

title: 08 asserts nothing and cannot run; 2.7's string-as-unsigned-integer rule and all of Table 2-2 are unproven, and the rule is BROKEN in VerA
detail: VERIFIED three ways. (1) `zig build torture -- ch02_lexical` reports 08 as CANNOT RUN — port-less, so nothing executes; it also carries no CHECK at all. (2) 2.7: 'A string literal used as an operand in expressions and assignments shall be treated as unsigned integer constants represented by a sequence of 8-bit ASCII values, with one 8-bit ASCII value representing one character', which makes every Table 2-2 row a derivable integer. (3) PROBED: `integer a; a = "AB";` compiles under --lint but the generated device fails to build with `invalid format string 'd' for type '*const [1:0]u8'` — VerA types every string literal as .string and never coerces. So this is a real VerA gap, and the fixture is the only thing that would record it. Merges uncovered's separate 2.7-operand, Table-2-2, spaces-in-strings and \ddd items into one file.
expected: Must-run with ports: `CHECKI("\\n is 10", "\n", 10)`, `CHECKI("\\t is 9", "\t", 9)`, `CHECKI("\\\\ is 92", "\\", 92)`, `CHECKI("\\\" is 34", "\"", 34)`, `CHECKI("a space is significant in a string", " ", 32)`, `CHECKI("AB is 16706", "AB", 16706)`, `CHECKI("A\\101 is 16705", "A\101", 16705)`. Add `//! xfail VerA types a string literal as .string and never coerces it to an integer operand (src/ir/lower.zig)` — which needs ch02-04. `//! lrm 2.7`, `//! lrm 2.3`.

title: 23 exercises the s-designator and asserts nothing — a compiler that ignores `s` and yields 15 passes today
detail: VERIFIED. torture reports 23 CANNOT RUN (port-less, CHECK-less). 2.6.1: 'the numbers specified with the base format shall be treated as signed integers if the s designator is included ... The s designator does not affect the bit pattern specified, only its interpretation ... Negative numbers shall be represented in 2's complement form', and Example 3 states the answers outright: `4 'shf` is "the 4-bit number '1111', to be interpreted as a 2's complement number, or '-1'" and `-4 'sd15` "is equivalent to -(-4'd 1), or '0001'". PROBED with a ported copy: VerA already yields -1, 1 and 15 correctly, so this is pure assertion debt, not a compiler gap — no xfail needed and it lands today.
expected: Rename off the historical `_rejected`. Ports plus: `CHECKI("4'shf is 1111 read as 2's complement", 4'shf, -1)`, `CHECKI("4'hf without s is unsigned", 4'hf, 15)`, `CHECKI("-4'sd15 is -(-4'd1)", -4'sd15, 1)`, `CHECKI("-8'd6 is a unary minus on the size constant", -8'd6, -6)`. `//! lrm 2.6.1`.

title: 22 assigns 'h837ff and asserts nothing; the unsized-constant value 538623 is fully derivable
detail: VERIFIED. torture reports 22 CANNOT RUN. 2.6.1: the size is optional, an unadorned base format is unsigned, and 'The number of bits that make up an unsized number ... shall be at least 32'. `'h837ff` = 0x837FF = 538623, MSB of the 32-bit value clear. Example 1 uses exactly this constant (`'h 837FF`). PROBED: VerA yields 538623 today, so this lands with no xfail.
expected: Rename off `_rejected`. Ports plus `CHECKI("unsized 'h837ff is at least 32 bits and unsigned", 'h837ff, 538623)` and `CHECKI("unsized 'o7460", 'o7460, 3888)` (Example 1's third line). `//! lrm 2.6.1`.

title: 21 was flipped to must-compile but left port-less and CHECK-less, so it scores CANNOT RUN and proves nothing
detail: VERIFIED. torture reports 21 CANNOT RUN. 2.9 Example 6 is `a = b + (* mode = "cla" *) c;` and A.8.3 admits `{ attribute_instance }` after a binary operator. The fixture writes `1.0 + (* mode = "cla" *) 2.0` and stops. The observable claim is that the attribute changes nothing about the arithmetic — which is the whole point of 2.9 ('properties ... used by various tools').
expected: Rename off `_rejected`. Ports plus `CHECKX("an attribute on a binary operator does not change the sum", 1.0 + (* mode = "cla" *) 2.0, 3.0)` and, for Example 8, `CHECKX("an attribute on ?: does not change the choice", 1 ? (* no_glitch *) 4.0 : 5.0, 4.0)` if 33_conditional_attribute.va does not already assert it. `//! lrm 2.9`, `//! lrm A.8.3`.

title: Left truncation and left zero-padding of a based constant are two-state arithmetic, work in VerA today, and are tested nowhere
detail: VERIFIED, and it disproves COVERAGE.md. 2.6.1: 'If the size of the unsigned number is smaller than the size specified for the constant, the unsigned number shall be padded to the left with zeros ... If the size of the unsigned number is larger than the size specified for the constant, the unsigned number shall be truncated from the left.' COVERAGE.md line 13 claims 'padding/truncation is therefore not representable in the device contract' because it lumps them in with x/z. That is false: PROBED and RAN — 2'd7 yields 3, 8'h1ff yields 255, 3'b1101 yields 5, all ok=1 under VerA today. The x/z half of the padding rule is genuinely out of scope (Annex C.3), the two-state half is not. 04_integer_bases.va's own header says so: 'Every one fits its declared size ... so none of them exercises the left-truncation rule.'
expected: New must-run fixture: `CHECKI("2'd7 truncates from the left to 3", 2'd7, 3)`, `CHECKI("3'b1101 truncates to 101", 3'b1101, 5)`, `CHECKI("8'h1ff truncates to ff", 8'h1ff, 255)`, `CHECKI("4'b1 pads left with zeros", 4'b1, 1)`, `CHECKI("16'h5 pads left with zeros", 16'h5, 5)`. `//! lrm 2.6.1`.

title: The DEBT banners on 05 and 24 defame a CONFORMANT rejection — Annex C.3 is the authority, not 2.6.1
detail: This is a CORRECTION of the negatives and weak lenses, both of which called these fixtures anti-conformant and asked for `//! xfail`. They are not. Annex C.3 (normative, annex-c-veriloga.html): 'From 2.6, Numbers: support for x and z values is limited in the analog block to the mixed signal context, as defined in 7.3.2. In the same paragraph, the use of the question mark character as an alternative for z is also limited to the mixed signal context.' VerA is a Verilog-A compiler and both fixtures put the literal in an analog block, so E0130 is the right answer and these are normative rejects, not debt. 24's own inline comment already says 'outside the Verilog-A subset' — it just sits under a banner that contradicts it. Leaving the banners in place mis-scores VerA in `zig build ledger` and would have cost two wrong rewrites.
expected: Delete the four-line DEBT banner from both. Replace with `//! lrm C.3` (plus `//! lrm 2.6.1` for the digit semantics) and a two-line comment quoting the Annex C.3 sentence. Keep `//! reject E0130`. Do NOT add `//! xfail`. Delete both .expected-error.txt sidecars.

title: Seven rejects pin prose where a stable code exists; two pin a single common English word that matches almost any diagnostic
detail: VERIFIED by reading each file and probing the real codes. 17_identifier_digit_rejected.va pins `//! reject identifier` — one word, matched against every message, point, title and note in the bag; probed, the real code is E0208. 18_system_whitespace_rejected.va pins `//! reject expression`; probed, E0209. 15 and 16 pin ``expected `;` ``, which any parse error satisfies. 12_unclosed_comment.va pins the bare phase label `ParseError` although src/diag_code.zig already carries E0102 'unterminated block comment'. 13 pins the prose fragment `module item`. 30 pins only `DiagnosticsReported`. README: 'Codes are the preferred form: they are stable ... and they pin WHICH rule fired rather than how it happened to be worded.'
expected: Replace each prose substring with the diagnostic code the fixture actually provokes (17 -> E0208, 18 -> E0209, 12 -> E0102, and the codes 13/15/16/30 emit today), and add the matching `//! lrm` cite. Where no specific code exists yet, say so in a comment rather than pinning a common word.

title: The ban on whitespace between the apostrophe and the base format character has no fixture
detail: VERIFIED. 2.6.1: 'The apostrophe character and the base format character shall not be separated by any white space.' PROBED: `4' h5` gives E0131 'expected a numeric base after the apostrophe', so VerA is already right — this is a missing fixture, not a gap. It is the exact complement of ch02-02 (whitespace AFTER the base is legal, whitespace INSIDE the base is not), and today the suite states the opposite of the LRM on both halves, so the two should land together.
expected: New reject fixture: `value = 4' h5;` with `//! reject E0131` and `//! lrm 2.6.1`.

title: x/z/? in a multi-digit DECIMAL constant is a prohibition with no fixture; the chapter's two x/z fixtures both target forms the LRM permits
detail: VERIFIED. 2.6.1: 'In a decimal constant, the unsigned number token shall not contain any x, z, or ? digits, unless there is exactly one digit in the token.' PROBED: `8'd1x` gives E0130, so VerA is right. Distinct from 05 and 24: those two reject single-digit and question-mark forms that 2.6.1 PERMITS and Annex C.3 merely puts out of the analog subset (see ch02-10); this one is an outright grammatical prohibition that holds in full Verilog-AMS too.
expected: New reject fixture: `value = 8'd1x;` with `//! reject E0130` and `//! lrm 2.6.1`. Comment must draw the contrast with 05/24 so a reader does not think it is a duplicate.

title: `.2e-7` — the fourth of the LRM's six named-invalid real forms — has no fixture
detail: VERIFIED. 2.6.2 lists six forms verbatim under 'The following are invalid forms of real numbers because they do not have at least one digit on each side of the decimal point': .12, 9., 4.E3, .2e-7, .1p, 34.M. Fixtures 14, 15 and 16 cover the first three. PROBED: `.2e-7` gives E0209. A reject fixture stops at its first diagnostic, so the three missing forms need three files, not one.
expected: New reject fixture: `value = .2e-7;` with `//! reject E0209` and `//! lrm 2.6.2`.

title: `.1p` — the fifth named-invalid real form, and the only one on the scale_factor branch — has no fixture
detail: VERIFIED. Same 2.6.2 list. PROBED: `.1p` gives E0209. Worth its own file because it is the only invalid-real example that goes down `unsigned_number [ . unsigned_number ] scale_factor` rather than the exp branch, so it is the one that would survive a lexer that special-cased exponents only.
expected: New reject fixture: `value = .1p;` with `//! reject E0209` and `//! lrm 2.6.2`.

title: `34.M` — the sixth named-invalid real form — has no fixture
detail: VERIFIED. Same 2.6.2 list. PROBED: `34.M` gives E0207 'unexpected token: found `.`' — a different code from its two siblings, which is itself worth pinning.
expected: New reject fixture: `value = 34.M;` with `//! reject E0207` and `//! lrm 2.6.2`.

title: 'No space is permitted between the number and the symbol' has no fixture
detail: SURVIVES BUT DOWNGRADED. 2.6.2, immediately under Table 2-1: 'No space is permitted between the number and the symbol.' The negatives lens rated this high on the claim that `1.3 u` 'silently yields 1.3e-6 and passes everything'. PROBED and that is FALSE — VerA gives E0207 'unexpected token: found u'. So the rule is honoured and only the fixture is missing; medium, not high.
expected: New reject fixture: `value = 1.3 u;` with `//! reject E0207` and `//! lrm 2.6.2`.

title: 'The first character of an identifier shall not be a digit or $' — only the digit half is tested
detail: VERIFIED. 2.8: 'The first character of an identifier shall not be a digit or $; it can be a letter or an underscore.' 17_identifier_digit_rejected.va covers the digit; nothing covers `$`. The gap matters because 2.8 also makes `$` LEGAL after the first character (`n$657`, exercised in 02_simple_identifiers.va), so the two rules interlock and only one side is pinned. PROBED: `real $gain;` gives E0208 'expected an identifier: found $gain'.
expected: New reject fixture: `real $gain;` with `//! reject E0208` and `//! lrm 2.8`.

title: 'A system_function_identifier or system_task_identifier shall not be escaped' has no fixture
detail: VERIFIED. Syntax 2-3 footnote 1: 'The $ character in a system_function_identifier, system_task_identifier, or system_parameter_identifier shall not be followed by white_space. A system_function_identifier or system_task_identifier shall not be escaped.' 18_system_whitespace_rejected.va covers the first sentence only. PROBED: `v = \$vt ;` gives E0314 'unknown identifier: `$vt`' — the right outcome (the escape makes it an ordinary name, which then does not exist) reached through a generic code.
expected: New reject fixture: `analog value = \$vt ;` with `//! reject E0314` and `//! lrm 2.8.3`. The comment must explain WHY E0314 is the conforming answer, or the next reader will 'fix' it.

title: 'Legal base specifications are d, D, h, H, o, O, b, or B' — no fixture tries an illegal letter
detail: VERIFIED. 2.6.1 names the eight legal spellings exhaustively. 35_uppercase_bases_hex.va proves all eight are accepted; nothing proves a ninth is not. PROBED: `8'y11` gives E0131. Cheap, and it is the negative that closes 35.
expected: New reject fixture: `value = 8'y11;` with `//! reject E0131` and `//! lrm 2.6.1`.

title: `4af` — the LRM's own Example 1 line labelled 'is illegal' — has no fixture
detail: VERIFIED. Example 1 of 2.6.1 is four lines and the fourth is `4af // is illegal (hexadecimal format requires 'h)`. PROBED: `value = 4af;` gives E0133 'invalid number literal: `4a`'. Distinct from ch02-20: that one has an apostrophe and a bad letter, this one has no apostrophe at all, and a lexer could plausibly get one right and the other wrong.
expected: New reject fixture: `value = 4af;` with `//! reject E0133` and `//! lrm 2.6.1`.

title: A zero size constant is illegal and VerA ACCEPTS it — a real conformance gap, not just a missing fixture
detail: VERIFIED, and this is the only new negative in the chapter that VerA currently fails. Syntax 2-2: `size ::= non_zero_unsigned_number`, and 2.6.1 repeats it in prose: 'It shall be specified as a non-zero unsigned decimal number.' PROBED: `value = 0'b1;` compiles clean under --lint, no diagnostic. The uncovered lens guessed this was likely an xfail because src/frontend/lexer.zig uses width==0 as the unsized sentinel; the probe confirms the symptom.
expected: New reject fixture: `value = 0'b1;` with `//! lrm 2.6.1`, the code the fix will emit, and `//! xfail VerA accepts a zero size constant; width 0 is the lexer's unsized sentinel`. This one works under today's runner because it is a reject fixture.

title: The four standard attributes have stated value domains, none of them enforced and none tested
detail: VERIFIED. 2.9.2: desc and units 'must be assigned a string'; op 'must be assigned a value, which must be either "yes" or "no"'; multiplicity 'must be assigned one of the following string values: "multiply", "divide", or "none"'. 11_attributes.va supplies only in-domain values. PROBED: `(* op="maybe" *)`, `(* multiplicity="sideways" *)` and `(* desc=7 *)` all compile with nothing but the unrelated W0650. Genuine unenforced rule.
expected: New reject fixture: `(* op = "maybe" *) parameter real x = 1.0;` with `//! lrm 2.9.2` and `//! xfail VerA does not check the value domain of the standard attributes`. Note the sibling violations (multiplicity, desc/units non-string) in the comment so the fix covers all four at once.

title: attr_spec's value is a constant_expression; VerA accepts a run-time variable
detail: VERIFIED. Syntax 2-4: `attr_spec ::= attr_name [ = constant_expression ]`. PROBED: `real z; (* q = z *) parameter real x = 1.0;` compiles clean. Low because nothing downstream reads attribute values in VerA, so the wrong acceptance is inert today.
expected: New reject fixture pinning a non-constant attribute value, with `//! lrm 2.9`, `//! lrm A.9.1` and `//! xfail VerA does not require an attribute value to be a constant expression`.

title: 2.9 enumerates exactly where an attribute may appear; no fixture tries a position outside the list
detail: VERIFIED. 2.9: 'An attribute_instance can appear ... as a prefix attached to a declaration, a module item, a statement, or a port connection. It can appear as a suffix to an operator or a Verilog-AMS function name in an expression' — a closed list, refined by Syntax 2-5..2-10. PROBED: `parameter real (* q *) x = 1.0;` gives E0208 and `v = 1.0 (* x *);` gives E0207, so VerA is already right. Low-medium: it is the negative that bounds ch02-08 and ch02-01, both of which widen where attributes are accepted, so it should land after them to stop the fix from over-shooting.
expected: New reject fixture: `parameter real (* q *) x = 1.0;` with `//! reject E0208` and `//! lrm 2.9`.

title: The dot-less exponent form is a distinct grammar branch and is unexercised; and one want uses CHECKR where 754 makes it bit-exact
detail: Two verified findings in one file. (1) real_number1's second alternative is `unsigned_number [ . unsigned_number ] exp [ sign ] unsigned_number` — the bracket makes the fraction OPTIONAL, and 2.6.2's own example list has `23E10` and `29E-2` with no dot. Every real in the chapter has a dot. PROBED and RAN: `23E10` yields 230000000000 exactly. (2) `CHECKR("decimal notation", decimal_value, 2.39426331e3, 1e-15)` — 1e-15 relative at 2394.26331 is 5.27 ulps, but 2.6.2 says reals 'are represented as described by IEEE Std 754' and 754 requires correctly-rounded decimal-to-binary conversion, so the two spellings are bit-identical. The file's other two wants already use CHECKX, so it is internally inconsistent.
expected: Change the first check to `CHECKX("decimal notation", decimal_value, 2394.26331)` and add `CHECKX("dot-less exponent", 23E10, 230000000000.0)` and `CHECKX("dot-less negative exponent", 29E-2, 0.29)`. `//! lrm 2.6.2`.

title: A scale factor on a FRACTIONAL mantissa — the LRM's own definition of scaled notation — is unexercised
detail: VERIFIED. 2.6.2 defines scaled notation with `24.7K, which indicates 24.7 multiplied by 10 to the third power`, and real_number1's third alternative is `unsigned_number [ . unsigned_number ] scale_factor`. Every one of 07's eleven rows uses the bare integer `1`, so the `[ . unsigned_number ]` half of that production is never taken. PROBED and RAN: `24.7K` yields 24700 exactly.
expected: Add `CHECKX("a scale factor applies to a fractional mantissa", 24.7K, 24700.0)` — the LRM's own example, digit for digit — and `CHECKX("1.3u", 1.3u, 1.3e-6)` from the same example list. `//! lrm 2.6.2`.

title: Syntax 2-8's two Verilog-A-reachable placements — block item declarations and analog function ports — are untested
detail: VERIFIED. Syntax 2-8 admits `{ attribute_instance }` on `function_port_list` tf_input_declarations and on every arm of `block_item_declaration`. COVERAGE.md's 2.9 row claims 31/21/32/33 'directly pin analog/expression placements' and waves the rest off as 'connection/UDP-only forms ... mixed/digital grammar boundaries' — but these two are neither: both are plain Verilog-A. PROBED: VerA accepts both today, so this is a pure coverage fixture.
expected: New must-run fixture: a named analog block with `(* desc="scratch" *) real v;`, and an analog function with `(* desc="argument" *) input x;`, plus a CHECKX proving the attributed declarations still hold their values. `//! lrm 2.9.1`, `//! lrm A.2.6`, `//! lrm A.2.8`.

title: The scale-factor alphabet is exactly eleven symbols with fixed case, and nothing proves a twelfth is refused
detail: VERIFIED. `scale_factor ::= T | G | M | K | k | m | u | n | p | f | a` — note K and k are the only pair, so every other letter's case is load-bearing. 07 proves all eleven are accepted. PROBED: `1g`, `1t`, `1P`, `1F`, `1A`, `1N`, `1U`, `1x` are all refused with E0207, so VerA is right. Also folds uncovered's separate 'exponent and scale factor are mutually exclusive' item: PROBED `1.0e3K` is refused too, which is what the grammar's `exp | scale_factor` choice requires.
expected: New reject fixture: `value = 1g;` with `//! reject E0207` and `//! lrm 2.6.2`; a second one for `1.0e3K` if the mutual-exclusion claim is worth its own file.

title: 'The underscore character is legal anywhere in a real constant except as the first character of the constant or the first character after the decimal point' — the second clause is untested
detail: VERIFIED. 2.6.2 states two underscore prohibitions and 34_real_underscores.va tests only the positive side. PROBED: `1._5` gives E0207. Small, but it is the only clause in 2.6.2 with a second exception nobody has written down.
expected: New reject fixture: `value = 1._5;` with `//! reject E0207` and `//! lrm 2.6.2`.

title: 'All keywords are defined in lowercase only' — nothing proves an uppercase spelling is an ordinary identifier
detail: VERIFIED. 2.8.2: 'All keywords are defined in lowercase only.' COVERAGE.md defers 2.8.2 to Annex B, but Annex B is an inventory of the lowercase spellings; it cannot state the case rule. 26_escaped_keyword.va covers the escape half of 2.8.2, not the case half. PROBED: `real REAL, MODULE, BEGIN;` compiles and they behave as ordinary variables.
expected: New must-run fixture declaring `real REAL, MODULE, BEGIN;` and asserting each holds its own value, e.g. `CHECKX("REAL is an identifier, not the keyword", REAL, 1.0)`. `//! lrm 2.8.2`.

title: An escaped identifier may be terminated by tab, newline or formfeed, and its charset is 33..126 — only space and `+` are ever tried
detail: VERIFIED. 2.8.1: 'Escaped identifiers shall start with the backslash character (\) and end with white space (space, tab, newline, or formfeed). They provide a means of including any of the printable ASCII characters in an identifier (the decimal values 33 through 126...).' 03 uses a space terminator and `+` only. PROBED: a tab-terminated escaped identifier is accepted, and so is the LRM's own `\***error-condition***` shape.
expected: Extend 03 with one tab-terminated escaped identifier and one wider-charset name from the LRM's example list (`\***err***`, `\{a,b}` or `\net1/\net2`), each with a CHECKX reading its value back. `//! lrm 2.8.1`.

title: `system_function_identifier ::= $ [ a-zA-Z0-9_$ ] { ... }` requires at least one character after the `$`
detail: VERIFIED. Syntax 2-3's A.9.3 productions make the character class after `$` mandatory. PROBED: `value = $ ;` gives E0209 'expected an expression: found invalid token'. Genuinely low value — it is one token off 18_system_whitespace_rejected.va — but it is cheap and closes the 2.8.3 grammar.
expected: New reject fixture: `analog value = $ ;` with `//! reject E0209` and `//! lrm 2.8.3`.

title: A compiler directive inside a comment is not a directive — the whole `//!` mechanism rests on it and nothing asserts it
detail: VERIFIED. 2.4 makes `//` run to end of line with no exception for the grave accent, and README leans on exactly this ('They survive the preprocessor untouched (§2.4 makes them comments)'). PROBED: a `` // `define X 1 `` line has no effect. 01 already carries the sibling claim that `//` has no meaning inside a block comment, so this is one more line in a file that is already about this.

title: The $vt header comment calls NIST2018 'Annex D's default'; the default is NIST1998. The DIGITS ARE RIGHT — do not move them
detail: THIS ITEM IS A CORRECTION OF THE LITERALS LENS, WHICH IS WRONG. The lens asserted that 'Annex D of VAMS 2.4 has FOUR sets, no NIST2018' and proposed moving the want to 0.0258520269036. VERIFIED AGAINST THE SHIPPED LRM and that is false: docs/VAMS-LRM/annex-d-stddefs.html defines `P_Q_NIST2018 1.602176634e-19` and `P_K_NIST2018 1.380649e-23` — exactly the pair the fixture names — so Annex D has FIVE sets and the fixture's count is right. The lens read a stale text extract. Moreover src/backend/codegen.zig:2522 hardcodes k/q = 8.617333262145179e-5, which is the NIST2018 ratio, so 300 * it = 0.025851999786435535 and the written want 0.0258519997864 is the bit-exact value VerA produces. Applying the lens's fix would have moved the want OFF the implementation and off a real Annex D set. The residual defect is one parenthetical: Annex D's `ifdef` chain falls through to NIST1998, commented 'use NIST1998 values as in LRM 2.2 - 2.3 for backwards-compatibility', so NIST2018 is a selectable set, not the default. Also dropped from the lens: the CHECKX($temperature, 300.0) complaint, which proposes no change and is exact under the harness's `//! temp 300`.
expected: One-word comment edit: 'the NIST2018 pair (Annex D's default, ...)' -> 'the NIST2018 pair (Annex D's newest set; the un-ifdef'd default is NIST1998, and the 1e-4 band covers all five)'. Keep the want 0.0258519997864 and the RTOL 1e-4 unchanged. Add `//! lrm 9.13` and `//! lrm D.2`.
